description.narrative:
Sverige har varit medlem i AFR100 sedan november 2020 och ingår i initiativets ledningsgrupp i 2022. Mellan december 2020 och februari 2023 bidrog Sverige med SEK 20 miljoner till initiativet, tillsammans med AUDA NEPAD och WRI som avtalspartners till Sida. Projektet implementerades enligt plan.
Det nya projektet som nu föreslås överensstämmer med Strategin för Sveriges regionala utvecklingssamarbete med Afrika 2022-2026. Projektet ska under den andra fasen med Sida-stöd till AFR100 ytterligare stärka arbetet med Land Accelerators Program, regional och nationell uppföljning av Forest Landscape Restoration, jämställhetsintegrering samt stöd till kommunikation och synlighet.

Sweden has been a member of AFR100 since November 2020 and has joined the Management Team of the iniative since 2022. From December 2020 to February 2023, Sweden contributed SEK 20 Million for the initiative in which AUDA-NEPAD and WRI were agreement partners of Sida. This project has been implemented as per the plan.
The newly proposed project is in line with the Swedish Regional Development Cooperation Strategy for Sub-Saharan Africa that runs from 2022-2026. The specific areas of intervention under the second phase of Sida support to AFR100 will be further supporting implementation of the Land Accelerators Program, strengthening regional and country level monitoring of Forest Landscape Restoration, Gender Mainstreaming as well as support for communications and visibility.

The Goal of the Project
Under this second phase of cooperation with SIDA, the AUDA-NEPAD/AFR100 Secretariat aims to accelerate the transition from commitments towards implementation by supporting the AFR100 countries in actualizing and scaling up their restoration commitments on the ground through various forest and landscape restoration actions.
The actualization of the countries restoration commitments will contribute to reversing the negative impacts of deforestation and environmental and land degradation, realize healthy, productive landscapes, enhance the livelihoods of smallholder and rural producers, and subsequently build the resilience of rural communities in Africa, who are most susceptible to risk factors.
Specific Objectives
1. Increased support to Women and Youth restoration entrepreneurs: Scaling up the Land Accelerator Programme (LAP).
2. Strengthening Community Resilience and Sustainable Land Restoration: Restore and protect ecosystems, increase carbon sequestration, increase water security, and soil fertility, provide more green jobs and incomes, improve food security and nutrition, and reduce migration.
3. Support to AFR100 Monitoring to crowd in and de-risk investment into FLR, build technical capacity in the country, create green tech jobs, and systematize AFR100 tracking and reporting.

title.narrative: Agreement with Annexes Sida-WRI AFR100 October 2023

description.narrative:
The WRI team in collaboration with the AFR100 secretariat achieved the following major milestones to expand the Land Accelerator across selected AFR100 member countries, establishing locally embedded National Chapters that have the capacity to replicate the program independently and reach even more entrepreneurs during the period October 1, 2023 September 30, 2024:
Key Achievements of the Land Accelerator Program (October 1, 2023 September 30, 2024)
- Expansion of the Land Accelerator Program: Successfully scaled up the program at the landscape level, partnering with five Business Development Service providers in Kenyas Great Rift Valley, Ghanas cocoa belt, and the Lake Kivu-Rusizi River landscape (Rwanda, Burundi, and DRC).
- Support for Entrepreneurs and Capacity Building: 106 restoration champions from 27 countries participated in the 2024 capacity-building program. 99 innovation grants were awarded to African entrepreneurs across AFR100 countries. 16 top-performing enterprises participated in an intensive one-week Boot Camp in Accra, Ghana, receiving targeted training and mentorship.
- Financial Support and Investment Mobilization: 33 Land Accelerator alumni secured over $7 million in funding from TerraFund through loans, equity, and grants. Strengthened investor engagement through Demo Day, where top 16 enterprises pitched their projects to key stakeholders.
- Networking, Peer Learning, and Knowledge Sharing: Facilitated peer-to-peer learning and mentorship to enhance business scalability and restoration impact. Hosted Demo Day in Accra, bringing together entrepreneurs, investors, and ecosystem stakeholders to foster partnerships. Organized field visits to restoration sites, showcasing best practices in sustainable landscape management.
- Monitoring and Support for AFR100 Implementation: Contributed to shaping the second State of AFR100 Report to refine impact tracking and improve forest restoration metrics. Prepared for the second AFR100 Landscape Monitoring Accelerator (scheduled for March 2025), supporting targeted countries in improving monitoring frameworks. activities related to the Regional Landscape Monitoring Accelerator were mostly planned for year 2 and year 3
- Lessons Learned and Risk Mitigation Strategies: Identified the need for in-country and landscape-specific programs to accommodate the large number of viable applicants. Addressed challenges in payment disbursement and program coordination by establishing a joint task force with AUDA-NEPAD. Recommended the creation of a Land Accelerator alumni network to foster continuous peer-to-peer support.
- Commitment to Gender and Social Equity: Strong focus on women and youth entrepreneurs, with 57% of co-founders in the program being women. Conducted outreach specifically targeting womens groups to increase participation in restoration enterprises. Implemented SEAH (Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment) assessment and mitigation measures to ensure program inclusivity and safety.
These achievements highlight the significant progress made in strengthening land restoration efforts, empowering entrepreneurs, and driving sustainable impact across AFR100 member countries.
